title: See Less, Enjoy More: The Biggest Travel Trends for 2027
paragraphs: Have you ever come home from a vacation feeling like you need another vacation?
Trying to visit every attraction, eat at every popular restaurant and do as much as possible can leave you very tired.
But in 2027, more travelers may decide that doing less is better. And instead of asking, "What do I want to see?" they may start asking, "How do I want to feel?"
That's one prediction in a new report from Lemongrass, a UK travel and tourism marketing company.

One of the main trends is the "anti-optimized vacation." Instead of packing every day with activities, travelers may choose simpler plans, stay longer in fewer places and leave more time for doing nothing at all.

That could also mean a move away from traditional "bucket lists." Rather than rushing from one place to another, people may want to spend more time learning about one place through its history, food and culture, or talking to locals.

Lemongrass also says that "near is the new far." Travelers may prefer trips within their own country, train journeys and even staycations — vacations spent at or near home — as they find they don't need to go far to feel like they've gotten away.

AI is also changing how people plan vacations, helping them choose where to go, what to do and what to expect. But as travelers become more careful about trusting AI, Lemongrass predicts they may place more value on recommendations from locals and people who have actually visited a destination.
Hotels may also pay more attention to lighting, noise and access to nature, creating spaces that help guests slow down and relax.
So perhaps the perfect vacation in 2027 won't be the one where you see everything.
It might be the one where you finally have nothing you need to do.
